portInfo.description: The Autoridad Portuaria de la Bahía de Cádiz publishes cruise facilities centred on the Terminal de Cruceros at Muelle Alfonso XIII: a recently renovated 1,300 m² terminal, quays advertised at 12 and 13 metres draught and 800 metres length with appropriate fenders, plus large bus and taxi parking and ship-supply installations. The dársenas technical table lists Alfonso XIII passenger cruise terminal at 180 m length, 10 m draught and 12,550 m², with La Galeona as a separate longer berth row. SeaDays keeps both primary figures visible. Commercial itineraries sometimes brand “Cádiz/Seville,” but Seville is an inland excursion from this port, not a second APBC cruise terminal in the fetched pages.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Photograph all-aboard before entering the old-town lane grid; Alfonso XIII is city-adjacent but not inside every alley.
